transcript.en: Hi, Joanna, good to meet you.
transcript.zh: 你好，Joanna，很高兴见到你。

transcript.en: Now, before we discuss your new research project, I'd like to hear something about the psychology study you did last year for your Master's degree.
transcript.zh: 在我们讨论你的新研究项目之前，我想听一听你去年读硕士的时候做过的心理学研究。

transcript.en: So how did you choose your subjects for that?
transcript.zh: 你当时是怎么选择的研究对象？

transcript.en: Well, I had six subjects, all professional musicians, and all female.
transcript.zh: 我有六个研究对象，全都是专业的音乐家，而且都是女性。

transcript.en: Three were violinists and there was also a cello player and a pianist and a flute player.
transcript.zh: 其中三位是小提琴家，还有一位大提琴演奏家，一位钢琴家和一位长笛演奏家。

transcript.en: They were all very highly regarded in the music world and they'd done quite extensive tours in different continents,
transcript.zh: 她们在音乐界声望都很高，而且在不同大洲还做过大量的巡回演出，

transcript.en: and quite a few had won prizes and competitions as well.
transcript.zh: 她们中不少还赢过一些奖项和比赛。

transcript.en: And they were quite young, weren't they?
transcript.zh: 而且她们还都相当年轻，对吧？

transcript.en: Yes, between 25 and 29 - the mean was 27.8.
transcript.zh: 是的，都在25-29岁之间，平均年龄是27.8。

transcript.en: I wasn't specifically looking for artists who'd produced recordings,
transcript.zh: 我本来并没有一定要找出过专辑的艺术家，

transcript.en: but this is something that's just taken for granted these days, and they all had.
transcript.zh: 但是最近这件事直接被当成理所当然的了，而且她们全都出过专辑。

transcript.en: Right. Now you collected your data through telephone interviews, didn't you?
transcript.zh: 好吧，你是通过电话采访收集的资料，对吗？

transcript.en: Yes. I realised if I was going to interview leading musicians it'd only be possible over the phone because they're so busy.
transcript.zh: 是的，我知道如果要采访这些重要的音乐家的话，就只能通过电话才有可能了，因为她们都特别忙。

transcript.en: I recorded them using a telephone recording adaptor.
transcript.zh: 我用一个电话录音转接器把跟她们的谈话内容录了下来。

transcript.en: I'd been worried about the quality, but it worked out all right.
transcript.zh: 我之前一直担心录音的音质，不过结果发现还不错。

transcript.en: I managed at least a 30-minute interview with each subject, sometimes longer.
transcript.zh: 我设法和每位研究对象进行了一段至少30分钟的采访，有的时间更长。

transcript.en: Did doing it on the phone make it more stressful?
transcript.zh: 通过电话采访有没有让你觉得压力更大？

transcript.en: I'd thought it might... it was all quite informal though and in fact they seemed very keen to talk.
transcript.zh: 我本来以为会这样没错......但是这些采访都没有那么正式，而且她们事实上似乎都很愿意谈话。

transcript.en: And I don't think using the phone meant I got less rich data, rather the opposite in fact.
transcript.zh: 我觉得用电话采访并不意味着我收集到的资料就没有那么多，实际上正好相反。

transcript.en: Interesting. And you were looking at how performers dress for concert performances?
transcript.zh: 有意思。你还研究了演奏家在音乐会上演出时的穿着？

transcript.en: That's right. My research investigated the way players see their role as a musician and how this is linked to the type of clothing they decide to wear.
transcript.zh: 没错，我研究调查了演奏者将她们自己定位成音乐家的方式，以及这和她们决定穿哪种服装有什么联系。

transcript.en: But that focus didn't emerge immediately.
transcript.zh: 但我并不是马上就想到了这一点。

transcript.en: When I started I was more interested in trying to investigate the impact of what was worn on those listening,
transcript.zh: 在研究最开始的时候，我对试着调查听众对她们穿的衣服的效果更加感兴趣，

transcript.en: and also whether someone like a violinist might adopt a different style of clothing from, say, someone playing the flute or the trumpet.
transcript.zh: 以及比如一位小提琴家是否会穿得跟长笛或者喇叭演奏者不同。

transcript.en: It's interesting that the choice of dress is up to the individual, isn't it?
transcript.zh: 每个人都有权选择他们的服装这件事还蛮有意思的，对吧？

transcript.en: Yes, you'd expect there to be rules about it in orchestras, but that's quite rare.
transcript.zh: 是的，我们原本以为管弦乐队对服装会有规定，但是这一现象非常少。

transcript.en: You only had women performers in your study.
transcript.zh: 你在研究时只选择了女性作为研究对象，

transcript.en: Was that because male musicians are less worried about fashion?
transcript.zh: 这是因为男性音乐家对时尚关心较少吗？

transcript.en: I think a lot of the men are very much influenced by fashion, but in social terms the choices they have are more limited...
transcript.zh: 我觉得很多男性都深受时尚的影响，但是从社会层面来看，他们在服装方面的选择更加有限，

transcript.en: they'd really upset audiences if they strayed away from quite narrow boundaries.
transcript.zh: 如果他们偏离了这本就狭窄的范围，会烦扰观众的。

transcript.en: Now, popular music has quite different expectations.
transcript.zh: 嗯，流行音乐对于服装方面的要求相当不同。

transcript.en: Did you read Mike Frost's article about the dress of women performers in popular music?
transcript.zh: 你读过Mike Frost关于流行女音乐家的穿着的文章吗？

transcript.en: No.
transcript.zh: 没有。

transcript.en: He points out that a lot of female singers and musicians in popular music tend to dress down in performance,
transcript.zh: 他指出很多流行音乐领域的女歌手和女音乐家往往在演出时穿得比较朴素，

transcript.en: and wear less feminine clothes, like jeans instead of skirts,
transcript.zh: 她们会穿不那么女性化的服装，比如相对于短裙，她们更愿意穿牛仔裤，

transcript.en: and he suggests this is because otherwise they'd just be discounted as trivial.
transcript.zh: 他提出这是因为如果不这么穿的话，她们就会被当成无足轻重的人物被忽视。

transcript.en: But you could argue they're just wearing what's practical...
transcript.zh: 但是我们也可以认为她们只是穿着比较实用的衣服......

transcript.en: I mean, a pop-music concert is usually a pretty energetic affair.
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，开一场流行音乐演唱会通常都需要很多精力。

transcript.en: Yes, he doesn't make that point, but I think you're probably right.
transcript.zh: 是啊，虽然他没有这么说，但是我觉得你可能是对的。

transcript.en: I was interested by the effect of the audience at a musical performance when it came to the choice of dress.
transcript.zh: 她们服装方面的选择在观看音乐表演的观众中起到的效果令我很感兴趣。

transcript.en: The subjects I interviewed felt this was really important.
transcript.zh: 我采访的这些研究对象都觉得这一点非常重要。

transcript.en: It's all to do with what we understand by performance as a public event.
transcript.zh: 这和我们对演出作为一种公开活动的理解有关系。

transcript.en: They believed the audience had certain expectations and it was up to them as performers to fulfil these expectations, to show a kind of esteem...
transcript.zh: 她们认为观众有某种期待，而这些期待需要她们作为表演者来满足，以表现出一种对观众的尊重。

transcript.en: ...they weren't afraid of looking as if they'd made an effort to look good.
transcript.zh: 她们并不担心自己看上去会像努力打扮过了一样。

transcript.en: Mmm. I think in the past the audience would have had those expectations of one another too,
transcript.zh: 我认为在过去，观众之间也互相存在期待，

transcript.en: but that's not really the case now, not in the UK anyway.
transcript.zh: 不过现在不是这样了，反正英国不是这样。

transcript.en: No.
transcript.zh: 是的。

transcript.en: And I also got interested in what sports scientists are doing too, with regard to clothing.
transcript.zh: 另外，我对运动科学家在服装方面的研究也产生了兴趣。

transcript.en: Musicians are quite vulnerable physically, aren't they, because the movements they carry out are very intensive and repetitive,
transcript.zh: 音乐家的身体相当脆弱，不是吗？因为他们做出的动作都很密集，而且时常重复，

transcript.en: I'd imagine some features of sports clothing could safeguard the players from the potentially dangerous effects of this sort of thing.
transcript.zh: 所以我猜运动类服装具有的一些性能能够保护演奏者在进行这种动作的时候不会受到潜在危险的影响。

transcript.en: Yes, but musicians don't really consider it.
transcript.zh: 是的，但是音乐家不太考虑这方面的问题。

transcript.en: They avoid clothing that obviously restricts their movements, but that's as far as they go.
transcript.zh: 她们只会避免穿着明显限制她们动作的服装，但是也就这样了。

transcript.en: Anyway, coming back to your own research, do you have any idea where you're going from here?
transcript.zh: 不管怎样，我们继续回到你自己的研究上来，你有没有想过这项研究接下来要怎么进行？

transcript.en: I was thinking of doing a study using an audience, including..
transcript.zh: 我想的是用一名观众做一项研究，包括......
